in_text_mentions: Skin examination revealed multiple erythematous annular and polycyclic plaques with central clearing and fine peripheral scaling on the trunk, proximal extremities, and face (Figures 1, 2). Some lesions showed superficial erosion and crusts; however, no intact vesicles or bullae were observed. There was no oral, ocular, or other mucous membrane involvement. General examination findings were unremarkable. Routine laboratory test results, including complete blood count, serum biochemistry, and antinuclear antibody testing, were within normal limits.
